newsitem.title: USA: Nellcor to buy Aequitron in stock swap.
newsitem.headline: Nellcor to buy Aequitron in stock swap.

text.p: Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc. has a definitive agreement to acquire Aequitron Medical Inc., another maker of respiratory products, in a stock swap worth about $61 million, the companies said Tuesday.

Minneapolis-based Aequitron makes electronic respiratory products for home health care and hospital use, wheelchair lifts and automobile hand controls. For the fiscal year ended April 30, 1996, it reported revenues of $38.5 million.
Nellcor, based in Pleasanton, Calif., is a major worldwide provider of products to monitor, diagnose and treat respiratory-impaired patients.

"Aequitron's product line is complementary to our own and includes a line of compact, portable ventilators which fills an important gap in our ventilator product line." said C. Raymond Larkin Jr., Nellcor president, in a statement.
After the acquisition, Nellcor will have the broadest ventilator line in the industry, he added.

Under the agreement, Nellcor will offer 0.432 share of its stock for each outstanding share of Aequitron in a tax-free pooling of interests. This is equivalent to $10.75 per Aequitron share, based on the Sept. 9 closing price of Nellcor, the companies said.
Aequitron's stock rose $1.25 to $10, while Nellcor was unchanged at $24.875 early on Nasdaq.
The exchange ratio is subject to adjustment based on the trading value of Nellcor shares for the 10-day period ending on the fifth trading day prior to a special meeting of Aequitron shareholders.
The acquisition is subject to approval by regulators and stockholders of Aequitron.
